title: Sorting Animals
source: Science G3 B1 Study sheet pp.7-9, Worksheet Q2-Q4, Q8

scenes.t: There are so many animals! Scientists sort them into groups by their food, their features and their habitat.
A herbivore eats only plants, like a cow, a rabbit or a giraffe.
A carnivore eats other animals, like a lion, a shark or an eagle.
An omnivore eats both plants and animals, like a bear, a chicken and… people!
Animals with a backbone are called vertebrates. Animals without a backbone are called invertebrates, like worms, insects and octopuses.
Vertebrates have five groups. Mammals have hair or fur and give birth. Birds have feathers, wings and beaks and lay eggs.
Fish have scales, fins and gills. Reptiles have dry scaly skin and lay eggs on land. Amphibians have wet soft skin and live in water and on land.

items.a: Eats only plants. Example: cow, rabbit.
Eats other animals. Example: lion, shark.
Eats plants and animals. Example: bear, chicken.
Have hair or fur, give birth, breathe with lungs.
Dry scaly skin, lay eggs on land.
Wet soft skin, live in water and on land, webbed feet.

activities.title: Backbone or Not?
activities.prompt: Does this animal have a backbone?

activities.title: Find Your Backbone
activities.goal: Feel your own backbone and test toy animals.

predict.q: Are you a vertebrate or an invertebrate?

steps.t: Bend forward slowly and ask a family member to gently run a finger down the middle of your back.
Can they feel little bumps in a line? Those are the bones of your backbone!
Now take your toy animals or pictures. Put the animals with a backbone in one group.
Put the animals without a backbone, like insects and worms, in another group.

activities.result: You can feel a line of small bones down your back. You are a vertebrate, like dogs, birds and fish!
activities.why: A backbone holds the body up. Invertebrates like worms and insects do not have one.
